problemStatement.formal: In an ultrametric space, d(x,z) <= max(d(x,y), d(y,z)), with geometric consequences for triangles and balls.
problemStatement.plain: Formalize the stronger non-Archimedean triangle inequality and its consequences for ultrametric geometry.
whyMatters: Explains the tree-like geometry of p-adic and non-Archimedean metric spaces
Shows how Mathlib ultrametric infrastructure implies familiar geometric corollaries

proven: The ultrametric inequality implies the standard triangle inequality.
Every ultrametric triangle is isosceles, with a sharp max-distance form when sides differ.
Mathlib ball and p-adic infrastructure supplies clopen-ball and non-Archimedean examples.
open: Formalize broader p-adic developments such as Ostrowski classification or Hensel-style applications.

insights: Replacing addition by max turns the triangle inequality into a much stronger geometric principle.
If two ultrametric side lengths differ, the third side equals the longer side.
Ultrametric balls behave like nested partitions: centers are not unique and balls can be clopen.
